## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
*Khambhakata* ("Hands on hips") is the twenty-first training rule (*sekhiya*) of the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga*, located in the Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. It forms part of the code of monastic etiquette regulating deportment in populated areas [SuttaCentral]. An English translation of the rule has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
Curated parallels recorded by SuttaCentral show an extensive transmission of this rule across diverse early Buddhist monastic traditions [SuttaCentral]. Within the Pali Vinaya, exact counterparts are preserved in the *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* (pli-tv-bu-pm-sk21), the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* (pli-tv-bi-vb-sk21), the *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* (pli-tv-bi-pm-sk21), and both the Bhikkhu and Bhikkhunī sections of the *Parivāra* [SuttaCentral]. Cross-tradition parallels are attested in Sanskrit, Classical Chinese, and Classical Tibetan across the Vinayas of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, and Kāśyapīya lineages [SuttaCentral].
Textual reuse analysis by DharmaNexus identifies 100 matching segments between this rule and 39 other Pali texts, reflecting the highly formulaic structure of the *Sekhiya* training rules [DharmaNexus]. The strongest phraseological overlaps occur with adjacent rules in the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga*, notably Sekhiya 23 (Bu-Vb Sk23; 1,060 matching characters across §0.1–1.9), Sekhiya 26 (Bu-Vb Sk26), and Sekhiya 22 (Bu-Vb Sk22) [DharmaNexus]. No cross-language alignments reach the threshold score of 10 in the automated DharmaNexus database [DharmaNexus].
